title: Rebuilding Quest for Glory II with AI: opening and character creator so far
author: prasithg
selftext:
I'm a lifelong engineer attempting my first game so please be gentle.  If you grew up pc gaming in the 90's i'm sure you heard of Sierra and Quest for Glory II was one of my favorite games growing up. I’m working on a browser-based fan rebuild, and this video shows the opening and character creation.

First of all this is freaking hard.  Just the intro and character creation and the play shell of the game took days and that is like 5% of the game.  I don't know how you see people on X or here with fully fleshed games out of prompts.  If you have some workflows then please share.

My process so far:

\- Researched the original screens, walkthroughs, music, and decompiled DOS scripts. Even character creation had details I’d forgotten: buying an unfamiliar skill costs 15 points for its first 5, and Honor/Communication aren’t part of the allocation pool.

\- Generated several art directions before building the interface. The welcome paintings are deliberately cinematic and aspirational, rather than examples of finished gameplay.

\- Used Hermes to coordinate Codex and Claude Code sessions for implementation, experiments, and review. I stayed involved in the visual direction and kept testing the experience.

\- Took AGDI soundtrack samples into Suno to develop the three tracks heard here, then matched them to the welcome, class selection, and allocation screens.

\- Generated short character animations and kept iterating. The Wizard initially looked like he was taking a deep sigh. The Thief needed to look more like he was sneaking. An inn painting went through several revisions before I chose a bazaar scene instead.

The music, artwork, and transitions took the most back-and-forth.

This is an unofficial fan experiment. Sierra’s original and AGDI’s remake have both been important references.

Would love feedback on the opening’s pacing and feel, especially from anyone who remembers the original. I wanted the opening to bring back that feeling of arriving in Shapeir and wondering what was waiting beyond the gates. Does it make you want to step into Shapeir again?
